title: Why we can't hear a dog whistle
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why can dogs hear a dog whistle but I can't?
What is the highest sound humans can hear?
Which animals hear the highest sounds?

explain.say: Pitch depends on how many times a sound wave vibrates each second, measured in hertz. A deep drum might be under 100 hertz; a tiny bird's whistle several thousand.

draw.text: Why we can't hear a dog whistle

explain.say: Young human ears hear from about 20 hertz up to about 20 thousand hertz. Higher than that is called ultrasound, and we simply cannot detect it.
A dog whistle blows a note above 20 thousand hertz, but dogs can hear up to about 45 thousand hertz. So the dog hears a clear whistle while you hear little or nothing.

Cats hear even higher, about 64 thousand hertz, and many bats over 100 thousand, because they hunt by very high sounds. Elephants are the opposite: their hearing tops out lower than ours but reaches far deeper rumbles.

faq.q: Why can dogs hear a dog whistle but I can't?
faq.a: A dog whistle makes a sound above about 20 thousand hertz, too high for human ears. Dogs can hear up to about 45 thousand hertz, so the whistle is easy for them to hear.
asks: How does a dog whistle work?
Why is a dog whistle silent?

faq.q: What is the highest sound humans can hear?
faq.a: About 20 thousand hertz for young people. The top limit drops with age, so many adults cannot hear sounds above 15 thousand hertz or so.
asks: What is the human hearing range?
Why can kids hear sounds adults can't?

faq.a: Ultrasound is sound with a pitch above about 20 thousand hertz, too high for humans to hear. Bats use it to hunt, and doctors use it to look inside the body.

faq.q: Which animals hear the highest sounds?
faq.a: Bats, dolphins and some moths hear the highest sounds, many well above 100 thousand hertz. Cats and mice also hear far higher than people.
asks: What animal has the best hearing?

faq.a: A hertz is one vibration per second. A sound of 440 hertz, the A that orchestras tune to, vibrates 440 times every second.

facts: Young humans hear roughly 20 to 20,000 hertz, and the upper limit falls with age.
Dogs hear up to about 45,000 hertz and cats up to about 64,000 hertz.
